template.name: lt-field
template.value: Enter your name.
template.description: Wires label, field, help text and error text together: sets `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid` on the control and an id on the help text and the error text. Never writes an id on the control: the template writes `for` and `id`, or wraps the field in the label. The field is invalid when the error text is there without `hidden`. Exists for markup produced without JavaScript. When the markup is produced with JavaScript, use `lt.field()` instead.

template.description: Tab list. The tabs are links to the panels in an `.lt-tabs__list`, so without JavaScript the list is a table of contents; `role="tab"` on anything other than a link is not a tab. The component adds keyboard and focus handling, sets roles and wiring, gives each panel its tab's name, makes only the selected panel a tab stop, and hides the rest with `hidden="until-found"`, so find in page and links into a panel reach them. Each selection is written to the URL. It never writes an id on a tab or a panel. When the page loads, the selected tab is the one with `aria-selected` from the server, otherwise the one the URL points to, otherwise the first one not hidden with `hidden`. Under `server-controlled` the URL never selects.

template.description: Field with a suggestion list. A `<label for>`, an `<input id>`, an `.lt-suggestion__list` with `<li>` items and a `[role=status]` are enough; the component sets the roles and the wiring where the markup came without them, and gives the list and the options ids. The field never gets an id from the component. Filters as the user types, moves the highlight with the arrow keys and announces the number of matches.

template.name: lt-session-timeout
template.value:
You will soon be logged out

We will log you out in to protect your information.
template.description: Warns before a signed-in session expires, and counts down. The renderer writes the dialog and the text inside the element: a `<dialog>` with `.lt-session-timeout__count` for the number, `[role=status]` for the announcement and the buttons in a `<form method="dialog">`. Dispatches `session-warn` when the dialog opens, `session-extend` when the user wants to continue, `session-logout` when the user logs out, `session-expired` when time is up, and `session-activity` at most once per `activity-interval` while the user is active, so the app can keep the server session alive.
